standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic conflict repair task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner identifies one real, still-unresolved disagreement or moment of friction with someone in the household from the recent past, builds a three-part repair statement for it, and has a short conversation aimed at resolving it.
safetyNotes: If a disagreement ever becomes unsafe rather than just uncomfortable, pause the conversation and get a trusted adult involved instead of continuing on your own.

Choose an everyday, low-stakes disagreement, such as chores, screen time, or a scheduling mix-up, rather than a deeper or more serious family issue; if the only unresolved friction you can think of feels heavier than that, use the simulation alternative instead.

simulationAlternative.description: If no suitable moment or unresolved friction is available to address directly this week, the learner instead writes out both sides of the repair conversation as an imagined script, including a realistic response from the other person and how the learner would react to that response.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain whether the conversation actually resolved the friction or just opened it up, and describe one thing you would do differently if you had the conversation again.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Repair statement structure: The statement names what happened, its effect on the learner, and one specific fix or next step. | Real conversation and agreement: The learner reports the real conversation, including the other person's response and any agreed next step. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner check back in with the same household member one week later about whether the agreed next step from the repair conversation actually happened, and record what they find.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic conflict repair task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: conflict repair worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner identifies one real, still-unresolved disagreement or moment of friction with someone in the household from the recent past, builds a three-part repair statement for it, and has a short conversation aimed at resolving it.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact conflict repair decision or action.
Model move 2: Think of one real disagreement or moment of friction with someone you live with that still feels unresolved.
Model move 3: Build a three-part repair statement: what happened from your side, how it affected you, and one specific fix or next step you are offering or requesting.

Model check: Repair statement structure: The statement names what happened, its effect on the learner, and one specific fix or next step. | Real conversation and agreement: The learner reports the real conversation, including the other person's response and any agreed next step.

resources.title: conflict repair action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for conflict repair.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: conflict repair coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner identifies one real, still-unresolved disagreement or moment of friction with someone in the household from the recent past, builds a three-part repair statement for it, and has a short conversation aimed at resolving it.
Coach direction: Think of one real disagreement or moment of friction with someone you live with that still feels unresolved.
Learner prompt: Describe what happened and why it still feels unfinished between you and the other person.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: conflict repair complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Build a three-part repair statement: what happened from your side, how it affected you, and one specific fix or next step you are offering or requesting.
Response 1 (t2-p1): My repair statement describes what happened without blaming the other person for everything.
Response 2 (t2-p2): My repair statement offers or requests one specific, doable next step, not just an apology.

Equal-access rule: If no suitable moment or unresolved friction is available to address directly this week, the learner instead writes out both sides of the repair conversation as an imagined script, including a realistic response from the other person and how the learner would react to that response.

resources.title: conflict repair minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain whether the conversation actually resolved the friction or just opened it up, and describe one thing you would do differently if you had the conversation again.

Success checks: Repair statement structure: The statement names what happened, its effect on the learner, and one specific fix or next step. | Real conversation and agreement: The learner reports the real conversation, including the other person's response and any agreed next step.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: conflict repair supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional conflict repair condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Repair statement structure: The statement names what happened, its effect on the learner, and one specific fix or next step. | Real conversation and agreement: The learner reports the real conversation, including the other person's response and any agreed next step..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guidedFirstAttempt.setup: The learner identifies one real, still-unresolved disagreement or moment of friction with someone in the household from the recent past, builds a three-part repair statement for it, and has a short conversation aimed at resolving it.

coachMoves: Ask the learner to name the condition.
Point to one model step only.

realRoute.title: conflict repair — permitted real-life route
realRoute.permissionRule: Use only a safe, permitted setting and the materials already available to you.
steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.
Build a three-part repair statement: what happened from your side, how it affected you, and one specific fix or next step you are offering or requesting.
Complete the response prompts on the delivered independent card without recording private identifying details.
Check the result against the delivered evidence record and correct any missed step.
realRoute.completionCondition: The learner submits the minimal process record and the completed application responses.

simulationRoute.title: conflict repair — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: If no suitable moment or unresolved friction is available to address directly this week, the learner instead writes out both sides of the repair conversation as an imagined script, including a realistic response from the other person and how the learner would react to that response.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Repair statement structure: The statement names what happened, its effect on the learner, and one specific fix or next step. | Real conversation and agreement: The learner reports the real conversation, including the other person's response and any agreed next step.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u04-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
